text:
maya (Platform): Heads-up — after the canary deploy to model-v2 this morning we started seeing a weird routing loop where requests that should've hit v2 ended up oscillating between v2 and the global fallback. Repro steps + logs below :eyes:

```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] req_id=abc123 eval_order=[policy:header-segment, policy:canary-percent, policy:global-fallback]
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] req_id=abc123 header X-User-Segment=beta -> match header-segment -> route to v2
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] req_id=abc123 route v2 returned 503 -> policy engine retries -> next eval -> global-fallback -> route to v1
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] req_id=abc123 cache_key mismatch -> re-eval -> matches header-segment again -> loop...
```

Config excerpt (from rollout manifest):
```
"routes": [
  {"name":"canary-percent","percent":5},
  {"name":"header-segment","header":"X-User-Segment","value":"beta"},
  {"name":"global-fallback","final":true}
]
```

samir (Runtime): @maya can you paste the full route trace for one req_id? Do we have retry-on-5xx enabled at the load-balancer or runtime? My hunch: retry policy + the order of route evaluation causes a re-evaluation that doesn't preserve a stable cache key (cookie/set-cookie from v2), so the engine keeps toggling. Also check if header rule has a stop_on_match/terminate flag.

ashley (SRE): I saw an SLO alert spike at 09:12 — increased error budget burn and p95 latency. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/route-eval (route_fallback_rate metric). :warning:

kai (Eng): Short mitigation options: reorder policies to evaluate header-based rule first and add `stop_on_match: true` to that rule, OR add a guard in the runtime to avoid re-evaluating the same request id more than once. Which is quicker to ship?

deploy-bot: canary deployment started: model-v2 @ 2026-03-18T09:10:00Z by @maya — canary id c-7821

tomas (Product): Any customer-facing impact? Need to know if we should banner status.

maya (Platform): Minimal customer impact seen so far (internal smoke failures + a small spike on stderr). Repro: `curl -H "X-User-Segment: beta" https://api.redwood/v1/generate` -> sometimes returns 503 then falls back to v1 and then the routing engine re-evaluates and flips back.

samir (Runtime): pushed a small runtime guard on branch `route-guard` that short-circuits if eval_count > 1 for same req_id. Patch snippet: 
```
if (evaluations_for(req_id) > 1) {
  log('route-loop-guard', req_id);
  return fallback_once();
}
```
PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4021 — running a canary of the runtime patch against 2 nodes now.

ashley (SRE): I've added temporary alerts and a throttle: if `route_fallback_rate` > 1% for the canary group, autoscale down the canary to 0% and page on-call. Metrics to watch: `route_eval_count`, `route_fallback_rate`, `request_latency_p95`. :gear:

kai (Eng): If the runtime fix looks good we should merge it, then follow up with a console UX change to expose `stop_on_match`/`finalize` toggle in the rollout UI so PMs/SEs can explicitly set it when creating header-based rules.

maya (Platform): Assigning @samir and @kai to follow up. Action items: rollback canary if metrics don't improve within 10m, merge route-guard if green, create UI ticket for rollout UX, and prepare a short postmortem if this affects broader SLOs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
